title: ADR-0087: the disposition section says `no-migration-prescription` is refused only by a body carrying a prescription; since PR #32649 it is also refused on a changeset declaring `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`
body:
domain:spec#2 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcSbLCxEmyHf9upz3pz

Filing gate: ① a governed text that no longer matches the gate it documents, owed by a landed PR (the `carrier:` line of the ACCEPT on PR #32649, comment 6819769601). ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the lane and grade.
Reader: `domain:skills` (`docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md`, a governed surface; Tier H).
Dedupe: `is:issue ADR-0087 no-migration-prescription narrowed` → none (#32601 is the gate card, closed by PR #32649).
reach: `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` on `origin/main` after `a8c761fb`: the disposition paragraph ("`no-migration-prescription` is refused by a body that carries a migration prescription", around line 764) and the category table row (around line 867: "refused — the body carries a FROM/TO block") name one refusal; the gate since #32649 (merge commit `a8c761fbe5ec06978f5e3582a35cf8be0c0503ae`) refuses the category a second way: on any changeset whose `breakingDeclaration` carries signal (5), a declared `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. An author or agent reading the ADR to pick a disposition for a narrowing reads that the catch-all is open to it.

## Business reason

The ADR is the text an author reads to choose a changeset marker; the gate is what refuses it. When they disagree, an author writes the marker the ADR allows and meets a refusal the ADR does not explain. The decision itself (seat decision A on #32601, under the not-escalated class "an existing gate's blind-spot repair") is already in force; this card only brings the governing text level with it.

## Ask

- In the disposition paragraph and the category table, add the second refusal: `no-migration-prescription` is refused on a changeset declaring `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (signal (5)), because a narrowing refuses something an author used to write and the upgrade guide is where an upgrading author learns it; the fix is a `registered` semantic entry, or a fact-checked category if one is true. Cite #32601 / PR #32649 as the source, in the ADR's own addendum style.
- No gate or vocabulary change (`CATEGORIES` is unchanged; `assertInputs`' ADR/CATEGORIES set check is unaffected).
